episodes.monthTheme: January, Identity: Who God Says I Am
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: For a long time, I believed I had to earn a place at the table — that God's love for me was a reward for good behavior I hadn't managed to produce yet. This week is about unlearning that. Being chosen was never about your performance. It was God's decision, made before your first mistake and unshaken by your worst one.

days.scripture: "But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light." (1 Peter 2:9, KJV)
days.truth: Being chosen was never about earning it — it was about God's initiative, not your performance.
days.affirmation: I am chosen by God, not because of what I have done, but because of who He is. My past does not disqualify me from His calling on my life.
days.sacredStep: Write down one lie you've believed about being "not chosen," and cross it out today.

days.scripture: "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit." (John 15:16, KJV)
days.truth: I didn't find God first. He pursued me long before I turned around.
days.affirmation: I am not chasing after worth I have to prove. God chose me before I ever chose Him, and that settles the question of my value.
days.sacredStep: Say out loud, "God chose me," before you leave the house today.

days.scripture: "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love." (Ephesians 1:4, KJV)
days.truth: My identity was decided before my worst season ever started.
days.affirmation: I am chosen from before the foundation of the world — my hardest year does not override a decision God made before I existed.
days.sacredStep: Read Ephesians 1 slowly and underline every phrase that describes who you are in Christ.

days.scripture: "But now thus saith the LORD that created thee... Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine." (Isaiah 43:1, KJV)
days.truth: God knows my name — not just my record.
days.affirmation: I am called by name, not by my mistakes. I belong to God, and nothing in my past changes whose I am.
days.sacredStep: Write your own name in the margin next to this verse today.

days.scripture: "Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering." (Colossians 3:12, KJV)
days.truth: Being chosen changes how I'm allowed to treat myself, not just how I treat others.
days.affirmation: I am God's elect, clothed in mercy and kindness — including mercy toward myself on the days I fall short.
days.sacredStep: Extend yourself one act of kindness today that you'd normally withhold.

days.scripture: "For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself." (Deuteronomy 7:6, KJV)
days.truth: Being chosen isn't a one- time event from the past. It's a present reality.
days.affirmation: I am set apart for God's purposes today, not because I am flawless, but because He has claimed me as His own.
days.sacredStep: Name one habit that doesn't match "set apart," and choose differently just once today.

days.scripture: "Knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God." (1 Thessalonians 1:4, KJV)
days.truth: Knowing I am chosen isn't pride. It's the peace that ends the arguing.
days.affirmation: I know, beloved, that I am chosen of God. That knowledge is the ground I stand on when doubt tries to pull me under.
days.sacredStep: Thank God specifically, out loud, for choosing you before you go to sleep tonight.

episodes.weeklyReflection: We started where every renewed identity has to start — with the fact that you were chosen before you had anything to offer. That's not a nice idea. It's the floor everything else in this book is built on. Next week, we go further: not just chosen, but loved in a way that refuses to be reduced to a label.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about being chosen stayed with me this week?
What was hardest to believe about being chosen before I had anything to offer?
What do I want to carry into next week about being chosen?

episodes.monthTheme: January, Identity: Who God Says I Am
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Addicts. Failures. Damaged. Broken. Somewhere along the way, most of us collected labels that felt more true than our own names. This week is about tearing those labels off one at a time and replacing them with the one word that was always underneath: beloved.

days.scripture: "Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God." (1 John 3:1, KJV)
days.truth: The label "son" or "daughter" was always underneath every other name I wore.
days.affirmation: I am a child of God, not a label the world or my own shame assigned me. That is the name that outlasts every other one.
days.sacredStep: Write "beloved child of God" somewhere you'll see it first thing tomorrow morning.

days.scripture: "I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee." (Jeremiah 31:3, KJV)
days.truth: God's love isn't a reaction to my recovery. It's the reason I have a recovery to walk.
days.affirmation: I am loved with an everlasting love — a love that existed before my struggle and will remain long after it.
days.sacredStep: List three things you've believed love had to be earned by, and set them down today.

days.scripture: "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us." (Romans 5:8, KJV)
days.truth: God didn't wait for me to clean up before He loved me.
days.affirmation: I was loved at my worst, not just my best. That means I don't have to perform to stay worthy of love now.
days.sacredStep: Recall one moment you felt "too far gone," and thank God He didn't agree.

days.scripture: "There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus." (Romans 8:1, KJV)
days.truth: Condemnation and conviction are not the same voice.
days.affirmation: I live free of condemnation. Christ's love does not come with a running tally of my failures attached.
days.sacredStep: Notice one condemning thought today and answer it out loud with this verse.

days.scripture: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?" (Romans 8:35, KJV)
days.truth: Nothing about my circumstances is powerful enough to unhook me from God's love.
days.affirmation: I am inseparable from the love of Christ — not my relapse, not my regret, not my worst day can move me out of His reach.
days.sacredStep: Name the hardest circumstance in your life right now, and speak this verse over it.

days.scripture: "Ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus." (Galatians 3:26, KJV)
days.truth: My family name was changed the day I put faith in Christ.
days.affirmation: I am a child of God by faith, not by feeling. Some days I won't feel it, and it will be true anyway.
days.sacredStep: Tell one trusted person today, "I'm learning to believe I'm loved, not labeled."

days.scripture: "The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy... he will joy over thee with singing." (Zephaniah 3:17, KJV)
days.truth: God isn't tolerating me. He is rejoicing over me.
days.affirmation: I am someone God sings over. That truth doesn't depend on how put-together my week looked.
days.sacredStep: Play or hum a worship song today and let it be a reminder that you're sung over, not just endured.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Labels are loud, but they aren't loyal — they'll leave the second you're not looking. Love, the kind we read about this week, doesn't move. Next week we take this a step further and talk about what happens to someone who is truly loved: they don't just feel different, they become different. New.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about being loved, not labeled stayed with me this week?
Which label did I try to set down this week, and what happened when I did?
What do I want to carry into next week about the name "beloved"?

episodes.monthTheme: January, Identity: Who God Says I Am
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: There's a version of you that existed before Christ got involved in your story, and there's a version that exists now. This week is about believing that the second version is actually real — not a performance, not wishful thinking, but a fact Scripture states plainly.

days.scripture: "Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new." (2 Corinthians 5:17, KJV)
days.truth: New isn't something I have to become someday. It's something I already am in Christ.
days.affirmation: I am a new creation. The old version of my life has passed away, even on the days my old habits try to argue otherwise.
days.sacredStep: Name one "old thing" you're ready to let stay in the past today.

days.scripture: "For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works." (Ephesians 2:10, KJV)
days.truth: I am not a finished product, but I am not a mistake either — I'm a work in progress made on purpose.
days.affirmation: I am God's workmanship, crafted with intention. My story is being written by a Creator who doesn't waste material.
days.sacredStep: Do one small "good work" today, even something private no one else will see.

days.scripture: "And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness." (Ephesians 4:24, KJV)
days.truth: Putting on the new man is a daily choice, not a one-time event.
days.affirmation: I put on the new man today. I choose the identity Christ gave me over the one addiction tried to assign me.
days.sacredStep: Before you dress this morning, say quietly, "I am putting on who Christ made me."

days.scripture: "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me." (Galatians 2:20, KJV)
days.truth: The old version of me isn't just hiding. It's dead, and something new took its place.
days.affirmation: I am alive in a way that isn't about my own strength anymore. Christ lives in me, and that changes what's possible for my day.
days.sacredStep: List one thing you're attempting today in your own strength, and hand it over in prayer.

days.scripture: "A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh." (Ezekiel 36:26, KJV)
days.truth: God doesn't patch the old heart. He replaces it, and what I assumed was permanent was never beyond His hands.
days.affirmation: I am not permanently defined by anything old. God is giving me a new heart, and what He is doing in me now is more real than what used to be true about me.
days.sacredStep: Write one "permanent" belief about yourself, then write "temporary" beside it.

days.scripture: "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby." (1 Peter 2:2, KJV)
days.truth: New creations grow slowly, and that's not a flaw in the process.
days.affirmation: I am growing, one small step at a time. I don't have to arrive today to be making real progress.
days.sacredStep: Read one short passage of Scripture today simply because it feeds you, not because it's a task.

days.scripture: "And he that sat upon the throne said, Behold, I make all things new. And he said unto me, Write: for these words are true and faithful." (Revelation 21:5, KJV)
days.truth: This promise comes with God's own signature on it. It is true and faithful, even on the days it doesn't feel that way.
days.affirmation: I am being made new by the One who keeps His word. I will keep reminding myself of this until it feels as real as it already is.
days.sacredStep: Write "Behold, I make all things new" on something you'll carry with you for the next seven days.

episodes.weeklyReflection: You are not who you used to be, even on the days it feels like nothing has changed. New creation isn't a metaphor — it's a fact you're learning to live inside of. Next week, we take a harder look at something that tries to convince you otherwise: your past.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about being made new stayed with me this week?
Where did I notice something new in me, even something small?
What do I want to carry into next week about what God is growing in me?

episodes.monthTheme: January, Identity: Who God Says I Am
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Shame has a way of turning your history into your identity, as if the worst thing you ever did is somehow the truest thing about you. This week draws a hard, necessary line between what happened to you and who you are.

days.scripture: "Forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before." (Philippians 3:13, KJV)
days.truth: Looking back constantly keeps me from walking forward at all.
days.affirmation: I am someone who is learning to release what's behind me. My past is part of my story, but it is not writing my future.
days.sacredStep: Name one memory you keep replaying, and consciously set it down today.

days.scripture: "As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us." (Psalm 103:12, KJV)
days.truth: God's removal of my past is total, not partial.
days.affirmation: My transgressions have been removed as far as the east is from the west. I don't have to keep dragging them back to myself.
days.sacredStep: Physically write down a past regret, then throw the paper away as an act of surrender.

days.scripture: "He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake." (Psalm 23:3, KJV)
days.truth: Restoration means God is doing something with the wreckage, not just ignoring it.
days.affirmation: My soul is being restored. What was damaged in my past is not the final word on my future.
days.sacredStep: Do one thing today that feels like caring for your own soul — rest, prayer, or quiet.

days.scripture: "Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more." (John 8:11, KJV)
days.truth: Jesus separates the person from the sin every single time.
days.affirmation: I am not condemned by my history. I am invited, like the woman in this story, to walk forward differently.
days.sacredStep: Read John 8:1-11 today and picture yourself as the one being spoken to.

days.scripture: "And such were some of you: but ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified." (1 Corinthians 6:11, KJV)
days.truth: "Such were" is past tense for a reason.
days.affirmation: I was some of those things. I am washed, sanctified, and justified now. My past tense does not get to become my present tense.
days.sacredStep: Speak this verse out loud over the specific past you're tempted to define yourself by.

days.scripture: "I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus." (Philippians 3:14, KJV)
days.truth: Pressing forward is possible even while carrying the memory of what's behind me.
days.affirmation: I am pressing toward what's ahead, not because my past didn't happen, but because it no longer gets to set the pace of my life.
days.sacredStep: Set one small forward-looking goal today, unrelated to your past mistakes.

days.scripture: "Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it?" (Isaiah 43:19, KJV)
days.truth: God is more interested in what's next than in rehearsing what's already happened.
days.affirmation: I am watching for the new thing God is doing in my life, even in the middle of an ordinary week.
days.sacredStep: Look for one small sign of growth in yourself today and name it out loud.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Your past is real. It happened. But it is not a life sentence, and it is not your identity — it's simply the road that brought you here. Next week, we come back to where this month began, standing fully in what it means to belong to God as His own child.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about my past not being my identity stayed with me this week?
What memory did I set down, even for a moment, and what was that like?
What do I want to carry into next week about letting go of the past?

episodes.monthTheme: January, Identity: Who God Says I Am
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: We close out January where identity always has to land: family. Not the family that abandoned you, or the family you disappointed, but the family that adopted you permanently, no matter what.

days.scripture: "But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name." (John 1:12, KJV)
days.truth: Becoming God's child was a gift I received, not a status I achieved.
days.affirmation: I am a child of God because I received Him, not because I earned a spot in His family through good behavior.
days.sacredStep: Say the word "received" out loud today as a reminder that grace was given, not earned.

days.scripture: "For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father." (Romans 8:15, KJV)
days.truth: Fear and shame are the language of bondage. Sonship speaks a different language entirely.
days.affirmation: I am adopted, not enslaved. I can call God "Father" instead of living under fear that never lets me rest.
days.sacredStep: Address your prayer today with the word "Father" and notice how it feels to say it.

days.scripture: "And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father." (Galatians 4:6, KJV)
days.truth: God didn't only name me His child. He put His Spirit in my heart to cry out "Father" when I can't find the words.
days.affirmation: I am God's child, and His Spirit speaks for me when my own words run out. His approval was always enough on its own.
days.sacredStep: Let go of one relationship's approval today that you've been chasing too hard.

days.scripture: "And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ." (Romans 8:17, KJV)
days.truth: An inheritance isn't earned through performance. It's received through relationship.
days.affirmation: I am an heir of God and a joint-heir with Christ. Whatever addiction stole from me, my inheritance in Him was never touched.
days.sacredStep: List one thing addiction took from you, and name what God's inheritance restores in its place.

days.scripture: "Like as a father pitieth his children, so the LORD pitieth them that fear him." (Psalm 103:13, KJV)
days.truth: God's posture toward me isn't frustration. It's compassion.
days.affirmation: I am shown compassion by a Father who understands my weakness better than I do, and loves me through it anyway.
days.sacredStep: Show yourself the same compassion today that this verse describes God showing you.

days.scripture: "And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty." (2 Corinthians 6:18, KJV)
days.truth: This promise was spoken directly, not vaguely, to me.
days.affirmation: I am His son or daughter by direct promise, not by accident or afterthought. He said it plainly, and I believe it today.
days.sacredStep: Read this verse aloud with your own name inserted where it says "sons and daughters."

days.scripture: "Ye are the children of the LORD your God." (Deuteronomy 14:1, KJV)
days.truth: Everything we've read this month builds toward this one simple sentence.
days.affirmation: I am the child of the Lord my God. Chosen, loved, made new, released from my past, and held as family — this is who I am.
days.sacredStep: Write one sentence summarizing what you now believe differently about your identity than you did on Day 1.

episodes.weeklyReflection: This month wasn't about becoming someone new by sheer effort. It was about recognizing who you already are in Christ — chosen, loved, made new, no longer defined by your past, and fully claimed as His child. Hold onto that identity, because next month we're going to need it. February is about grace, and grace only makes sense to someone who already knows they're loved enough to receive it.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about being God's child stayed with me this week?
What changes when I think of God as a Father who calls me His own?
What do I want to carry into next week about being God's child?
Keep one verse close. Choose the one that landed hardest this month and put it somewhere you'll see it first thing in the morning.
Answer the label out loud. When a shame- label shows up, say your verse back to it. Just once is enough to start.
Tell one person. Share one thing you now believe differently about yourself. Being known is part of being healed.

episodes.monthTheme: February, Grace: Releasing Shame & Guilt
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Guilt, when it's doing its job, points you toward repentance and then lets go. But a lot of us have carried guilt long after it finished its job, dragging it around like proof we're not allowed to move on. This week is about letting grace finally outweigh it.

days.scripture: "But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound." (Romans 5:20, KJV)
days.truth: No amount of guilt is bigger than the grace available to cover it.
days.affirmation: I am covered by a grace that is greater than every mistake I have ever made. My guilt does not get the final vote.
days.sacredStep: Name the guilt you've carried longest, and speak this verse directly over it.

days.scripture: "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God." (Ephesians 2:8, KJV)
days.truth: Grace was never something I could earn my way into, which means I can't disqualify myself out of it either.
days.affirmation: I am saved by grace, a gift I didn't earn and can't lose through failure. My worst day doesn't cancel a gift already given.
days.sacredStep: Write the word "gift" somewhere visible today as a reminder grace isn't a wage.

days.scripture: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness." (1 John 1:9, KJV)
days.truth: Confession isn't punishment. It's the door grace walks through.
days.affirmation: I am cleansed when I confess, fully and completely, not partially or on a delay. God's forgiveness doesn't come with fine print.
days.sacredStep: Confess one specific thing to God today, out loud, and receive His answer as final.

days.scripture: "Who is he that condemneth? It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us." (Romans 8:34, KJV)
days.truth: Guilt that lingers after confession is condemnation, not conviction. The only One with the right to condemn me is the One praying for me.
days.affirmation: I live without condemnation. If a voice keeps punishing me after I've already been forgiven, it isn't the voice of my Father. Christ is interceding for me right now.
days.sacredStep: Identify one thought pattern today that sounds like condemnation, and name its true source.

days.scripture: "I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins." (Isaiah 43:25, KJV)
days.truth: God's forgetting is intentional, not passive.
days.affirmation: I am forgiven so completely that God chooses not to remember what I keep bringing back up. I can choose to release it too.
days.sacredStep: Practice not bringing up an old failure today, even in your own head, even once.

days.scripture: "The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy." (Psalm 103:8, KJV)
days.truth: God's default posture toward me is mercy, not anger waiting to be provoked.
days.affirmation: I am met with mercy, not a short fuse. God's patience with me is deeper than my patience with myself.
days.sacredStep: Extend the same patience to yourself today that this verse describes God extending to you.

days.scripture: "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness." (2 Corinthians 12:9, KJV)
days.truth: Weakness isn't disqualifying. It's actually where grace does its clearest work.
days.affirmation: I am not disqualified by my weakness. Grace is sufficient for exactly the places I feel least capable.
days.sacredStep: Name one weakness you've hidden out of shame, and hand it to God in prayer today.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Guilt wants to keep score forever. Grace closes the book the moment you bring it honestly to God. This week was about letting the second one win. Next week, we go after something that clings even tighter than guilt: shame itself.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about grace outweighing guilt stayed with me this week?
Where did I notice guilt that had already done its job and was still hanging around?
What do I want to carry into next week about grace and guilt?

episodes.monthTheme: February, Grace: Releasing Shame & Guilt
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Guilt says "I did something wrong." Shame says "I am something wrong." This week is about telling the difference — and refusing to let shame speak over an identity that grace has already settled.

days.scripture: "They looked unto him, and were lightened: and their faces were not ashamed." (Psalm 34:5, KJV)
days.truth: Shame loses its grip the moment my focus shifts from myself to God.
days.affirmation: I am someone whose face does not have to stay covered in shame. When I look to God, shame loses the last word.
days.sacredStep: Look up, literally, and say this verse out loud the next time shame surfaces today.

days.scripture: "And Adam and his wife were both naked, and were not ashamed." (Genesis 2:25, KJV)
days.truth: Shame entered the story after the fall. It was never part of who I was originally created to be.
days.affirmation: I was not created for shame. It's an intruder in my story, not a permanent resident.
days.sacredStep: Name one area where shame has moved in uninvited, and mark it as "not mine to keep."

days.scripture: "For thou art my hope, O Lord GOD: thou art my trust from my youth." (Psalm 71:5, KJV)
days.truth: My trust doesn't have to be in my own record. It can rest in God instead.
days.affirmation: I am trusting God with my history, not trying to manage my own reputation anymore. That's a weight I no longer have to carry.
days.sacredStep: Release one attempt today to control how someone else sees your past.

days.scripture: "Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed: neither be thou confounded; for thou shalt not be put to shame." (Isaiah 54:4, KJV)
days.truth: God speaks directly against shame, not just against sin.
days.affirmation: I am told plainly not to be ashamed. That instruction is for me too, not just for people whose stories look cleaner than mine.
days.sacredStep: Say "I will not be put to shame" out loud once today, even if it feels unfamiliar.

days.scripture: "Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed." (Romans 10:11, KJV)
days.truth: Belief and shame cannot both hold the same seat at the same time.
days.affirmation: I am believing on Christ, and that belief is actively displacing shame, even on the days it feels slow.
days.sacredStep: Replace one shame-filled thought today with a specific truth about Christ.

days.scripture: "And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness... but that which is through the faith of Christ." (Philippians 3:9, KJV)
days.truth: I was never meant to build my own righteousness to hide my shame behind.
days.affirmation: I am found in Christ's righteousness, not my own performance. That means shame has nothing to attach itself to anymore.
days.sacredStep: Let go of one attempt at self-improvement today that was really about hiding shame, not healing.

days.scripture: "For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind." (2 Timothy 1:7, KJV)
days.truth: Shame often disguises itself as fear of being truly known.
days.affirmation: I have a sound mind, not a fearful one. I can be known fully without being defined by what shame wants me to hide.
days.sacredStep: Tell one safe person one true thing today that shame has kept you from saying out loud.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Shame convinces you that exposure equals destruction. Every day this week said otherwise — you can be fully seen and still be fully loved. Next week, we test that truth against one of the hardest experiences in recovery: the relapse.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about shame and guilt stayed with me this week?
When did I hear the difference between "I did something wrong" and "I am something wrong" this week?
What do I want to carry into next week about shame's lies?

episodes.monthTheme: February, Grace: Releasing Shame & Guilt
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: If you've relapsed — in addiction, in anger, in an old pattern you thought you'd left behind — this week is written specifically for you. Grace was never designed only for the person who never falls. It was designed for the one who gets back up.

days.scripture: "For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again." (Proverbs 24:16, KJV)
days.truth: Falling is not the opposite of righteousness. Staying down is.
days.affirmation: I am someone who gets back up. A fall doesn't erase the progress I've made — it's simply part of the road I'm walking.
days.sacredStep: If you've fallen recently, get back up in one specific, practical way today.

days.scripture: "Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me." (Psalm 51:10, KJV)
days.truth: After a relapse, I don't have to wait until I feel clean to ask. David prayed this prayer from the middle of his mess.
days.affirmation: I am free to ask God for a clean heart today, plainly and without delay, without first proving I've learned my lesson.
days.sacredStep: Pray this verse out loud today, word for word, even if it feels too simple.

days.scripture: "Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow." (Isaiah 1:18, KJV)
days.truth: God isn't interested in shaming me back into obedience. He's inviting me to reason with Him honestly.
days.affirmation: I am invited into honest conversation with God, not an interrogation. He already knows, and He's still reaching toward me.
days.sacredStep: Talk to God today the way this verse describes — honestly, without performance.

days.scripture: "The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way. Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down." (Psalm 37:23-24, KJV)
days.truth: A fall was never the same thing as being cast down permanently.
days.affirmation: I am not utterly cast down by my fall. God's hand is still on my steps, even the ones that stumbled.
days.sacredStep: Take one ordered step forward today, however small, as evidence you're not staying down.

days.scripture: "Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings." (Jeremiah 3:22, KJV)
days.truth: The invitation after a backslide is to return, not to disappear in shame.
days.affirmation: I am invited to return, not banished for straying. Healing is offered the moment I turn back.
days.sacredStep: Return to one practice you abandoned during your relapse — prayer, a meeting, a habit — today.

days.scripture: "Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit." (Psalm 51:12, KJV)
days.truth: Restoration is God's specialty, especially with the soul that feels most worn down. Joy can be restored, and so can the strength to keep going.
days.affirmation: I am being restored, not discarded. A setback does not disqualify me from the process God is already running, and He will uphold me through it.
days.sacredStep: Do one act of soul-care today that isn't about proving your worth, just about resting in it.

days.scripture: "And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten." (Joel 2:25, KJV)
days.truth: God specializes in restoring time, not just moments.
days.affirmation: I believe God can restore what relapse cost me — not just forgive it, but actually give back what was lost.
days.sacredStep: Name one thing relapse cost you, and ask God specifically to restore it.

episodes.weeklyReflection: If this week found you in the middle of a fall, hear this clearly: grace was never reserved for people who never stumble. It's for you, right now, exactly where you are. Next week, we widen the lens even further — grace isn't just for the relapse. It's for everything.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about grace after a fall stayed with me this week?
If I stumbled this week, what small step back did I take? If I didn't, what do I want to remember on a hard day?
What do I want to carry into next week about coming back instead of hiding?

episodes.monthTheme: February, Grace: Releasing Shame & Guilt
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: We close out February with the widest possible view of grace — not grace for one category of failure, but grace big enough to cover the whole story, past, present, and future.

days.scripture: "And of his fulness have all we received, and grace for grace." (John 1:16, KJV)
days.truth: Grace isn't rationed. It's given in continuous, overlapping supply.
days.affirmation: I am receiving grace for grace — a fresh supply for every new need, not a limited amount I might run out of.
days.sacredStep: Ask God for grace specifically for whatever today's challenge turns out to be.

days.scripture: "But he giveth more grace... God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble." (James 4:6, KJV)
days.truth: Humility, not perfection, is what positions me to receive more grace.
days.affirmation: I am humble enough to admit I need more grace today than I did yesterday, and that admission is exactly where grace meets me.
days.sacredStep: Admit one specific need for grace to God or to another person today.

days.scripture: "And God is able to make all grace abound toward you." (2 Corinthians 9:8, KJV)
days.truth: "All grace" leaves nothing out — not one category of my life is excluded.
days.affirmation: I am covered by all grace, in every area — my finances, my relationships, my recovery, my thought life. None of it is outside His reach.
days.sacredStep: Name one area of your life you assumed grace didn't apply to, and invite it in today.

days.scripture: "For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ." (John 1:17, KJV)
days.truth: I'm not living under a system that measures my worth by performance.
days.affirmation: I am living under grace and truth, not law and record-keeping. Christ changed the terms of the whole relationship.
days.sacredStep: Notice one moment today you slip back into performance mode, and consciously choose grace instead.

days.scripture: "And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power." (Colossians 2:10, KJV)
days.truth: Completeness in Christ isn't something I'm working toward. It's already a fact.
days.affirmation: I am complete in Him. Grace didn't leave part of me unfinished, waiting on my own effort to fill the gap.
days.sacredStep: Rest, on purpose, from one form of striving today, trusting completeness is already true.

days.scripture: "Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need." (Hebrews 4:16, KJV)
days.truth: Boldness, not hesitation, is the posture grace invites me into.
days.affirmation: I am welcome to come boldly, not timidly, into God's presence — even on my hardest, most ashamed day.
days.sacredStep: Pray boldly today about the thing you'd normally approach God about hesitantly.

days.scripture: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all." (Revelation 22:21, KJV)
days.truth: Grace was Scripture's closing word for a reason — it's meant to be the last thing you're left holding.
days.affirmation: I am held by grace, from the first page of my story to the last. Nothing about February has been wasted.
days.sacredStep: Write one sentence describing how your understanding of grace has shifted this month.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Grace was never small enough to fit into one category of your story — it covers your guilt, your shame, your relapse, and every unnamed thing you haven't found the words for yet. You're not carrying this alone anymore. Next month, we build on that foundation by learning what it means to actually trust the God who gave it.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about grace for all of me stayed with me this week?
Which area of my life did I assume grace didn't reach, and what would it mean to let it in?
What do I want to carry into next week about how far grace reaches?
Confess without delay. When something is on your conscience, say it to God plainly and early, not after days of carrying it.
Name the voice. When a thought sounds like shame, ask, "Is this conviction or condemnation?" and answer with a verse.
Return quickly. If you stumble, take one small step back the same day instead of waiting until you feel worthy.
episodes.nextWeekTitle: Trusting God With What I Can't Control

episodes.monthTheme: March, Faith: Learning to Trust God
episodes.weekTitle: Trusting God With What I Can't Control
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: So much of addiction and shame is built on trying to control the uncontrollable — outcomes, other people, your own cravings, your own past. This week is about releasing that grip, one finger at a time.

days.scripture: "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding." (Proverbs 3:5, KJV)
days.truth: My own understanding was never a strong enough foundation to lean my whole weight on.
days.affirmation: I am trusting God with all my heart today, not just the parts I can rationalize or control.
days.sacredStep: Name one thing you're white- knuckling right now, and consciously loosen your grip on it.

days.scripture: "Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee." (Psalm 55:22, KJV)
days.truth: Carrying it myself was never a requirement. It was a habit.
days.affirmation: I am someone who casts my burden instead of carrying it alone. God sustains what I release to Him.
days.sacredStep: Say out loud one specific burden you're handing over today.

days.scripture: "Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass." (Psalm 37:5, KJV)
days.truth: Committing my way doesn't mean I stop moving. It means I stop demanding to see the whole path.
days.affirmation: I am committing my way to God today, trusting Him with the outcome instead of trying to engineer it myself.
days.sacredStep: Take one action today aligned with faith, without needing proof it will work first.

days.scripture: "What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee." (Psalm 56:3, KJV)
days.truth: Fear and trust can exist in the same moment — trust doesn't require the absence of fear.
days.affirmation: I am afraid sometimes, and I trust God anyway. Those two things are allowed to coexist in the same day.
days.sacredStep: Name your current fear honestly to God, and choose to trust Him in spite of it.

days.scripture: "For we walk by faith, not by sight." (2 Corinthians 5:7, KJV)
days.truth: Needing to see the outcome before I trust means I'm not actually trusting yet.
days.affirmation: I am walking by faith, not by what I can currently see. My next step doesn't require full visibility.
days.sacredStep: Take one step today that requires trust, not certainty.

days.scripture: "Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you." (1 Peter 5:7, KJV)
days.truth: God's care for me isn't passive. It's active enough to hold what I hand over.
days.affirmation: I am cared for, actively and personally, which means my care doesn't have to be self-managed anymore.
days.sacredStep: Identify one area of over-functioning today, and consciously hand a piece of it to God.

days.scripture: "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God." (Philippians 4:6, KJV)
days.truth: I'm invited to bring my anxious thoughts to God instead of carrying them alone.
days.affirmation: I am bringing my anxious thoughts into prayer instead of letting them run unmanaged in my own head.
days.sacredStep: Turn one anxious thought today directly into a spoken prayer.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Control was never actually keeping you safe — it was just keeping you exhausted. This week began the slow work of putting your hands down. Next week, we look at the hardest place to trust God at all: the waiting.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about releasing control stayed with me this week?
What did I try to hold tight this week, and what did loosening my grip feel like?
What do I want to carry into next week about loosening my grip?

episodes.monthTheme: March, Faith: Learning to Trust God
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Waiting is where a lot of recovery actually happens — waiting for healing, for restored relationships, for a life that finally feels different. This week is about staying faithful in the space between the prayer and the answer.

days.scripture: "Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD." (Psalm 27:14, KJV)
days.truth: Waiting is repeated twice in this verse because it's hard enough to need saying twice.
days.affirmation: I am waiting with courage, not despair. Strength is being built in me during this season, even when it doesn't feel like progress.
days.sacredStep: Name one thing you're waiting on, and thank God for the strength being built in you now.

days.scripture: "But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles." (Isaiah 40:31, KJV)
days.truth: Waiting isn't wasted time. It's the process through which strength gets renewed.
days.affirmation: I am renewing my strength in this waiting season. What feels stalled is actually preparation for what's ahead.
days.sacredStep: Rest intentionally today instead of forcing progress that isn't ready yet.

days.scripture: "I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry." (Psalm 40:1, KJV)
days.truth: Patience in waiting isn't passive resignation — it's active trust that God is listening.
days.affirmation: I am being heard, even in the silence. My patience is not going unnoticed by God.
days.sacredStep: Voice one prayer today you've been repeating, and trust that it has been heard.

days.scripture: "For yet a little while, and he that shall come will come, and will not tarry." (Hebrews 10:37, KJV)
days.truth: Delay is not the same thing as denial.
days.affirmation: I am confident that what God has promised is coming, even if it hasn't arrived on my preferred timeline.
days.sacredStep: Write down one promise you're waiting on, dated today, as an act of expectant faith.

days.scripture: "Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him." (Psalm 37:7, KJV)
days.truth: Rest and waiting are meant to go together, not waiting anxiously while refusing to rest.
days.affirmation: I am resting in the Lord during this wait, not striving to force an outcome ahead of schedule.
days.sacredStep: Choose one form of genuine rest today instead of anxious striving.

days.scripture: "It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD." (Lamentations 3:26, KJV)
days.truth: Quiet waiting is described here as good — not weak, not wasted.
days.affirmation: I am doing something good by waiting quietly instead of forcing a resolution before it's ready.
days.sacredStep: Practice quiet — literal silence — for five minutes today as an act of trust.

days.scripture: "And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not." (Galatians 6:9, KJV)
days.truth: Due season is a real promise, even when it feels indefinitely delayed.
days.affirmation: I am not fainting in this season. My due season is coming, even if today doesn't show me the harvest yet.
days.sacredStep: Keep doing one good, small thing today that you're tempted to give up on.

episodes.weeklyReflection: The waiting season isn't empty — it's where faith gets its muscle. You're not behind. You're being built. Next week, we take that built-up faith and put it face-to-face with the thing that most often shuts it down: fear.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about waiting stayed with me this week?
What am I still waiting on, and what got me through the hardest moment of waiting?
What do I want to carry into next week about waiting well?

episodes.monthTheme: March, Faith: Learning to Trust God
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Fear and faith both ask you to believe in something you can't fully see. This week is about choosing which voice you'll actually listen to.

days.scripture: "For I the LORD thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee." (Isaiah 41:13, KJV)
days.truth: Fear can visit me without being my master. God doesn't just tell me not to be afraid. He takes my hand while He says it.
days.affirmation: I am held by the God who says, "I will help thee." That help belongs to me even when I can't feel it.
days.sacredStep: Name a specific fear today, then hold out your hand and pray this verse over it out loud.

days.scripture: "The LORD is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?" (Psalm 118:6, KJV)
days.truth: Fear doesn't disqualify me from trusting God. Remembering whose side He's on is often the first step through it.
days.affirmation: I am not facing this alone. The LORD is on my side, and I am choosing trust in the middle of fear, not waiting for fear to disappear first.
days.sacredStep: Do one thing today you'd normally avoid out of fear, in a small, manageable way.

days.scripture: "There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear." (1 John 4:18, KJV)
days.truth: Love, not willpower, is what actually removes fear over time.
days.affirmation: I am being loved by a perfect love that is slowly casting out every fear I've carried.
days.sacredStep: Sit with God's love for a few quiet minutes today instead of trying to talk yourself out of fear.

days.scripture: "Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God." (Isaiah 41:10, KJV)
days.truth: Presence, not the absence of hard circumstances, is what this promise actually offers.
days.affirmation: I am not alone in what I'm afraid of. God's presence is the antidote fear can't argue with.
days.sacredStep: Speak this verse over your current situation, by name, today.

days.scripture: "I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears." (Psalm 34:4, KJV)
days.truth: I can go back to the same God about the same fear. He heard me then, and He hears me now.
days.affirmation: I am heard whenever I seek the LORD, including the tenth time I bring the same fear to Him.
days.sacredStep: Identify a fear that keeps returning, and tell God about it again today, on purpose.

days.scripture: "The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?" (Psalm 27:1, KJV)
days.truth: The question in this verse isn't rhetorical for effect — it's meant to actually be asked.
days.affirmation: I am asking myself honestly, "whom shall I fear?" and finding the answer smaller than I thought.
days.sacredStep: Ask that question out loud about your biggest current fear today.

days.scripture: "Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed." (Joshua 1:9, KJV)
days.truth: Courage was commanded, which means it's available, not just hoped for.
days.affirmation: I am commanded to be strong and courageous — not because I feel ready, but because God has already equipped me.
days.sacredStep: Take one courageous step today that this month's fear has been holding back.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Fear will keep showing up — that's not a sign you're failing at faith. What matters is which voice gets the final word each time. Next week, we finish this month by looking at something encouraging: God doesn't need a big faith to do a big work.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about fear stayed with me this week?
When fear showed up, what did I do with it, and what helped?
What do I want to carry into next week about meeting fear?

episodes.monthTheme: March, Faith: Learning to Trust God
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: This week closes out March with good news for anyone who feels like their faith is too small to matter: it was never about the size of your faith. It's about the size of who you're placing it in.

days.scripture: "If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove." (Matthew 17:20, KJV)
days.truth: A mustard-seed amount of faith was described as sufficient, not insufficient.
days.affirmation: I am not disqualified by small faith. Even the smallest amount, placed in the right God, is enough to move mountains.
days.sacredStep: Name your "mountain," and pray with the small faith you actually have, not the faith you wish you had.

days.scripture: "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief." (Mark 9:24, KJV)
days.truth: Belief and doubt can be spoken in the same sentence and still count as real faith.
days.affirmation: I am allowed to believe and still ask for help with my unbelief. That honesty is not a failure of faith — it is faith.
days.sacredStep: Pray this exact verse today, word for word, about whatever you're doubting.

days.scripture: "According to your faith be it unto you." (Matthew 9:29, KJV)
days.truth: God meets me where my actual faith is, not where I think it should be.
days.affirmation: I am met by God according to the faith I have today, however small that feels.
days.sacredStep: Pray one honest, small prayer today instead of a performed, "bigger" one.

days.scripture: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen." (Hebrews 11:1, KJV)
days.truth: Faith doesn't require visible proof to be real substance.
days.affirmation: I am holding onto substance, not wishful thinking. My hope has weight, even when it's invisible to everyone else.
days.sacredStep: Write down one thing you're hoping for that you haven't yet seen come true.

days.scripture: "For with God nothing shall be impossible." (Luke 1:37, KJV)
days.truth: The size of the impossibility has never been the real question. God's ability has always been the answer.
days.affirmation: I am trusting a God for whom nothing is impossible, including the specific thing I've labeled hopeless.
days.sacredStep: Name your "impossible," and speak this verse directly over it today.

days.scripture: "Without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is." (Hebrews 11:6, KJV)
days.truth: Simply believing God exists and is at work is already a meaningful act of faith.
days.affirmation: I am pleasing God simply by believing He is real and active in my life, even before I see results.
days.sacredStep: Thank God today just for being present, without asking for anything else first.

days.scripture: "Great is thy faithfulness." (Lamentations 3:23, KJV)
days.truth: My faith doesn't have to be great for God's faithfulness to already be great.
days.affirmation: I am relying on God's faithfulness, which was always bigger than the size of my own belief.
days.sacredStep: List three ways God has already proven faithful in your recovery, no matter how small.

episodes.weeklyReflection: You don't need a bigger faith. You need the same small faith, aimed at the same big God, repeated every day. That's enough. Next month, we take that trust and put it to work breaking the strongholds that trust alone hasn't fully loosened yet.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about small faith stayed with me this week?
Where did a small, honest prayer make a difference this week?
What do I want to carry into next week about small faith?
Name what you're gripping. Each morning, say the one thing you're most tempted to control, and hand it to God out loud.
Pray the honest prayer. When doubt shows up, use Mark 9:24: "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief."
Keep a "hitherto" list. Write down one way God has helped you each week. It builds a record you can read when the waiting gets long.

episodes.monthTheme: April, Freedom: Breaking Strongholds
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: You can't tear down a wall you refuse to name. This week is about honest identification — not shame, not self- condemnation, just clear-eyed truth about what's actually holding you.

days.scripture: "For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds." (2 Corinthians 10:4, KJV)
days.truth: I'm not fighting this battle with willpower alone — the weapons available to me are spiritual, and they work.
days.affirmation: I am equipped with weapons mighty enough to pull down strongholds. This fight was never meant to be fought with willpower alone.
days.sacredStep: Name one specific stronghold honestly, out loud or in writing, for the first time today.

days.scripture: "Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God." (2 Corinthians 10:5, KJV)
days.truth: Strongholds often start as a single repeated thought before they become a whole fortress.
days.affirmation: I am learning to notice the thought before it becomes the fortress. Awareness is the first sacred step toward freedom.
days.sacredStep: Catch one recurring lie-filled thought today and name it as exactly that — a lie.

days.scripture: "The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe." (Proverbs 18:10, KJV)
days.truth: There's a difference between the strongholds that trap me and the tower that protects me.
days.affirmation: I am running toward God's strong tower, not the fortress addiction built for me. That direction matters more than my speed.
days.sacredStep: Choose God's "tower" over an old coping pattern once today, even in a small moment.

days.scripture: "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?" (1 Corinthians 3:16, KJV)
days.truth: The place a stronghold occupies was never meant to be its permanent territory — it belongs to something else entirely.
days.affirmation: I am God's temple. Every stronghold occupying that space is trespassing, not a permanent tenant.
days.sacredStep: Reclaim one specific space, habit, or hour of your day for God today.

days.scripture: "Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you." (James 4:7, KJV)
days.truth: Resistance without submission rarely lasts — the order in this verse matters.
days.affirmation: I am submitted to God first, which gives my resistance actual power instead of just willpower running on empty.
days.sacredStep: Submit one specific struggle to God in prayer before trying to resist it in your own strength.

days.scripture: "The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life." (John 10:10, KJV)
days.truth: A stronghold's purpose is always destruction, dressed up as relief or comfort.
days.affirmation: I am choosing life over the counterfeit relief a stronghold has offered me for years.
days.sacredStep: Name what a stronghold actually costs you, honestly, in one sentence today.

days.scripture: "If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed." (John 8:36, KJV)
days.truth: Freedom "indeed" implies there's a counterfeit version too — one worth telling apart from the real thing.
days.affirmation: I am being made free indeed, not just temporarily relieved. That's a different, deeper kind of freedom than I've settled for before.
days.sacredStep: Write down what "free indeed" would look like practically in your life, this week.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Naming a stronghold honestly is not weakness — it's the first act of real courage in this fight. You can't defeat what you refuse to see clearly. Next week, we move from naming the chains to believing they're actually broken.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about naming my stronghold stayed with me this week?
What did it feel like to name it out loud or on paper?
What do I want to carry into next week about honesty about my strongholds?

episodes.monthTheme: April, Freedom: Breaking Strongholds
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: This week is for the part of you that still braces like the chains are intact, even after Christ has already broken them. It's time to actually walk like it.

days.scripture: "Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage." (Galatians 5:1, KJV)
days.truth: Freedom already given still requires me to stand in it, not passively wait for it to feel true.
days.affirmation: I am standing fast in the liberty Christ already secured for me, refusing to pick the old yoke back up out of habit.
days.sacredStep: Identify one old "yoke" you keep instinctively reaching for, and set it down again today.

days.scripture: "Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son:" (Colossians 1:13, KJV)
days.truth: My freedom was a transfer carried out by someone else. I was moved into a new kingdom, and I didn't earn the ticket.
days.affirmation: I am free because I have been moved, not because I worked my way out. I live in the kingdom of God's dear Son now.
days.sacredStep: Thank God specifically today for freedom you didn't earn.

days.scripture: "For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace." (Romans 6:14, KJV)
days.truth: Dominion has already changed hands, even if old habits still act like the previous owner is in charge.
days.affirmation: I am not under sin's dominion anymore. Its old authority over me expired the moment I came under grace.
days.sacredStep: Speak "you no longer have dominion" over your specific struggle today.

days.scripture: "He hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives... to set at liberty them that are bruised." (Luke 4:18, KJV)
days.truth: Deliverance was explicitly part of the mission, not an afterthought.
days.affirmation: I am one of the captives this verse was written for. Liberty was always part of the plan for my life.
days.sacredStep: Read this verse today as if it were addressed to you personally, because it was.

days.scripture: "He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and brake their bands in sunder." (Psalm 107:14, KJV)
days.truth: The bands were broken, not loosened. Some truths need to be said more than once before they sink all the way in.
days.affirmation: I am rehearsing my freedom today until it feels as real as it already is. What was broken in two does not get put back together.
days.sacredStep: Say "He broke my bands in sunder" three times today, at three different points in your day.

days.scripture: "For when ye were the servants of sin... But now being made free from sin, and become servants to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness." (Romans 6:20-22, KJV)
days.truth: A change of servitude happened, not just a change of behavior.
days.affirmation: I am no longer serving what used to own me. My allegiance changed, and my daily choices are starting to catch up.
days.sacredStep: Serve something today — a person, a task, a prayer — that reflects your new allegiance.

days.scripture: "Ye are bought with a price; be not ye the servants of men." (1 Corinthians 7:23, KJV)
days.truth: A price was already paid, which means I don't need to keep paying for my own freedom through shame or striving.
days.affirmation: I am bought with a price I could never afford myself. That transaction is finished, not ongoing.
days.sacredStep: Rest today from one habit of trying to "earn" a freedom that's already fully paid for.

episodes.weeklyReflection: The chains aren't slowly loosening — they're already broken. What's slowly changing is your posture, learning to walk like a free person instead of bracing like a prisoner. Next week, we look specifically at one of the strongest chains many of us carry: addiction's grip.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about freedom already given stayed with me this week?
Where did I pick up an old yoke out of habit, and how did I set it back down?
What do I want to carry into next week about standing in freedom?

episodes.monthTheme: April, Freedom: Breaking Strongholds
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: This week names addiction directly — not to shame it, but to speak truth over its specific, persistent grip.

days.scripture: "But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection." (1 Corinthians 9:27, KJV)
days.truth: The body's cravings are not the highest authority in my life, even when they feel loudest.
days.affirmation: I am learning to bring my body into subjection to God's Spirit, not the other way around.
days.sacredStep: When a craving surfaces today, pause and name it out loud before responding to it.

days.scripture: "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof." (Romans 6:12, KJV)
days.truth: Obeying a craving is a choice, even when it doesn't feel like one in the moment.
days.affirmation: I am choosing what reigns in my body today. Addiction doesn't get automatic obedience anymore.
days.sacredStep: Identify one moment today you'll likely be tempted, and plan your response in advance.

days.scripture: "There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful... but will with the temptation also make a way to escape." (1 Corinthians 10:13, KJV)
days.truth: An escape route exists every single time, even when I can't see it yet.
days.affirmation: I am being given a way of escape with every temptation, whether or not I've spotted it yet.
days.sacredStep: Identify your "way of escape" for today's most likely temptation, ahead of time.

days.scripture: "For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace." (Romans 8:6, KJV)
days.truth: What I feed my mind determines the direction my whole day moves.
days.affirmation: I am setting my mind on things that lead to life and peace, not the things that once led to destruction.
days.sacredStep: Replace one piece of media or content today that feeds carnal thinking with something that feeds your spirit.

days.scripture: "Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak." (Matthew 26:41, KJV)
days.truth: Willingness of spirit doesn't erase weakness of flesh — that's exactly why watchfulness and prayer both matter.
days.affirmation: I am watching and praying, honest about my flesh's weakness without letting it define the outcome.
days.sacredStep: Set a specific reminder today to pray at the hour you're historically most vulnerable.

days.scripture: "For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness... we should live soberly." (Titus 2:11-12, KJV)
days.truth: Grace doesn't just forgive relapse — it actively trains me toward something different.
days.affirmation: I am being taught by grace itself how to live soberly, one day at a time, not just forgiven after the fact.
days.sacredStep: Ask God specifically today to teach you, not just to forgive you.

days.scripture: "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me." (Philippians 4:13, KJV)
days.truth: The strength for "all things" was never meant to come from my own resolve alone.
days.affirmation: I am strong enough for today, not because of my willpower, but because Christ's strength is doing the heavy lifting.
days.sacredStep: Say this verse before the moment you expect to be tested today, not just after.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Addiction's grip loses power the moment it's named, watched for, and met with a plan instead of surprise. You're not fighting this blind anymore. Next week, we turn to a quieter stronghold — one that doesn't look like addiction but binds just as tightly: people-pleasing.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about addiction's grip stayed with me this week?
What was my plan for my hardest moment, and who did I let know about it?
What do I want to carry into next week about my plan for hard moments?

episodes.monthTheme: April, Freedom: Breaking Strongholds
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Some strongholds are loud. This one is quiet — built from a lifetime of managing other people's opinions of you instead of resting in God's. This week is about laying that particular burden down.

days.scripture: "For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ." (Galatians 1:10, KJV)
days.truth: Serving Christ and constantly managing everyone's approval can't both be my top priority.
days.affirmation: I am seeking to please God, not to manage everyone's opinion of me. Those two goals were never actually compatible.
days.sacredStep: Name one relationship where you've been managing approval instead of living honestly, and adjust one small thing today.

days.scripture: "The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe." (Proverbs 29:25, KJV)
days.truth: What feels like caring what people think is often actually fear wearing a socially acceptable disguise.
days.affirmation: I am safe when I trust God's opinion of me more than the fear of what others might think.
days.sacredStep: Do one small thing today you'd normally avoid out of fear of others' opinions.

days.scripture: "Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?" (Galatians 4:16, KJV)
days.truth: Telling the truth sometimes costs approval, and that cost is survivable.
days.affirmation: I am willing to tell the truth even when it risks someone's approval. Honesty matters more than being liked.
days.sacredStep: Say one honest thing today that you've been softening or avoiding to keep the peace.

days.scripture: "But of these who seemed to be somewhat... God accepteth no man's person." (Galatians 2:6, KJV)
days.truth: Status and reputation don't influence how God sees me, so they shouldn't run my whole life either.
days.affirmation: I am not defined by how important or impressive I appear to others. God's acceptance was never about my image.
days.sacredStep: Let go of one attempt today to appear more impressive than you actually feel.

days.scripture: "Ye are the light of the world... let your light so shine before men." (Matthew 5:14-16, KJV)
days.truth: Being seen isn't the problem — living to be seen is.
days.affirmation: I am free to be visible without needing everyone's applause. My light doesn't require universal approval to matter.
days.sacredStep: Do one good thing today without telling anyone about it.

days.scripture: "If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men." (Romans 12:18, KJV)
days.truth: Peace with everyone was never actually promised or possible — only what depends on me is my responsibility.
days.affirmation: I am responsible for my own peace-seeking effort, not for controlling how every relationship ultimately lands.
days.sacredStep: Release responsibility today for one relationship's outcome that isn't yours to control.

days.scripture: "Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men." (Colossians 3:23, KJV)
days.truth: Working "as to the Lord" changes my whole motivation structure.
days.affirmation: I am doing my work and living my life as unto God, not as a performance for an audience I'll never fully satisfy.
days.sacredStep: Reframe one task today as an offering to God instead of a performance for others.

episodes.weeklyReflection: People-pleasing is exhausting precisely because it's an audience that never stops moving the target. God's approval doesn't move. This week began the shift from performing to resting. Next week, we bring everything this month together and talk about what freedom looks like as a daily practice, not just a moment of deliverance.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about people-pleasing stayed with me this week?
When did I check someone's approval before God's, and what did I do instead?
What do I want to carry into next week about God's approval?

episodes.monthTheme: April, Freedom: Breaking Strongholds
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Deliverance is often a moment. Freedom is a daily walk. This final week of April is about what it looks like to actually live free, one ordinary day at a time.

days.scripture: "This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh." (Galatians 5:16, KJV)
days.truth: Freedom is maintained by an active, daily walk, not a single decision made once.
days.affirmation: I am walking in the Spirit today, one deliberate choice at a time, not coasting on a decision I made in the past.
days.sacredStep: Choose one Spirit-led action today instead of your default reaction.

days.scripture: "If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit." (Galatians 5:25, KJV)
days.truth: Living free and walking free are two different things that have to match.
days.affirmation: I am aligning how I walk with what I already believe about who I am in Christ.
days.sacredStep: Notice one gap today between what you believe and how you're acting, and close it.

days.scripture: "Only let your conversation be as it becometh the gospel of Christ." (Philippians 1:27, KJV)
days.truth: Freedom shows up in ordinary conversation, not just big moments of victory.
days.affirmation: I am letting my everyday words reflect the freedom I'm walking in, not just my big declarations.
days.sacredStep: Pay attention to your words today and let one conversation reflect your freedom on purpose.

days.scripture: "Stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong." (1 Corinthians 16:13, KJV)
days.truth: Standing fast is an active posture, required daily, not a one-time stance.
days.affirmation: I am standing fast today, choosing strength again even though I already chose it yesterday.
days.sacredStep: Identify where you need to "stand fast" specifically today, and do it.

days.scripture: "And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me." (Luke 9:23, KJV)
days.truth: Jesus said "daily" on purpose. Freedom's daily practice can feel repetitive without ever being wasted.
days.affirmation: I am following one ordinary day at a time. The daily, unglamorous choices are exactly what a free life is built from.
days.sacredStep: Do one unglamorous, freedom- maintaining task today without needing it to feel exciting.

days.scripture: "Take heed to thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee." (1 Timothy 4:16, KJV)
days.truth: Continuing matters as much as starting.
days.affirmation: I am continuing what I started, even on the days motivation runs low. Consistency is its own kind of victory.
days.sacredStep: Continue one habit today purely because you started it, not because you feel like it right now.

days.scripture: "And I will walk at liberty: for I seek thy precepts." (Psalm 119:45, KJV)
days.truth: Freedom is a fact and a daily walk. Liberty and seeking God's Word show up in the same sentence.
days.affirmation: I am walking at liberty, and I am learning what that looks like one ordinary day at a time.
days.sacredStep: Write down one specific way your daily life looks different now than it did on April 1st.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Freedom was never meant to be a one-time event you look back on nostalgically — it's a walk, repeated daily, that slowly becomes who you are. This month named the strongholds, believed the chains were broken, and practiced living that out. Next month, we turn to something freedom makes possible: real healing in the places that are still broken.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about daily freedom stayed with me this week?
What small, ordinary thing did I do this week that belongs to a free person?
What do I want to carry into next week about ordinary freedom?
Keep your escape plan in writing. Write down your most vulnerable time of day and what you will do when it arrives.
Say the verse before the test. Don't wait until after. Speak John 8:36 at the start of a hard hour.
Check in on schedule. Choose one person and one regular time to tell the truth about how you're doing.

episodes.monthTheme: May, Healing: Restoring the Broken Places
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Before healing can begin, it has to be seen honestly. This week is about letting God into the places you've hidden even from yourself.

days.scripture: "He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds." (Psalm 147:3, KJV)
days.truth: My brokenness isn't hidden from God, and it isn't too much for Him.
days.affirmation: I am seen in my broken places, and I am being healed there, not judged for having them.
days.sacredStep: Name one broken place honestly to God today that you've avoided naming before.

days.scripture: "The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit." (Psalm 34:18, KJV)
days.truth: God draws closer, not farther away, when I'm at my most broken.
days.affirmation: I am not abandoned in my brokenness. God moves nearer exactly when I feel least deserving of closeness.
days.sacredStep: Invite God's nearness today into the specific area that feels most broken right now.

days.scripture: "A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench." (Isaiah 42:3, KJV)
days.truth: God's gentleness with weak, barely-holding-on things is deliberate, not accidental.
days.affirmation: I am handled gently by God, even when I feel like a bruised reed. He isn't looking for a reason to finish breaking me.
days.sacredStep: Treat yourself with the same gentleness this verse describes, at least once today.

days.scripture: "Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?" (Psalm 56:8, KJV)
days.truth: My pain has been noticed and recorded, not dismissed as unimportant.
days.affirmation: I am not crying unnoticed. Every tear I've cried has mattered to God, even the ones no one else ever saw.
days.sacredStep: Allow yourself to feel one emotion honestly today instead of pushing it down.

days.scripture: "For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive; and plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon thee." (Psalm 86:5, KJV)
days.truth: Being seen by God comes with mercy attached, not exposure and shame.
days.affirmation: I am met with mercy the moment I call out, not judgment for needing to call out at all.
days.sacredStep: Call on God specifically today about the broken place you named this week.

days.scripture: "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end." (Jeremiah 29:11, KJV)
days.truth: What I assume God thinks about my wreckage and what He actually thinks are often very different things.
days.affirmation: I am the subject of thoughts of peace, not condemnation. God's plan for my broken places is restoration, not punishment.
days.sacredStep: Write down what you assume God thinks about your struggle, then correct it with this verse.

days.scripture: "Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting." (Psalm 139:23-24, KJV)
days.truth: Inviting God to search me is safer than letting shame do the searching alone.
days.affirmation: I am inviting God into every corner, trusting Him to lead me toward healing rather than condemnation.
days.sacredStep: Pray this exact prayer today, slowly, meaning every word.

episodes.weeklyReflection: Being seen was the scariest and most necessary part of this week. God didn't recoil from what He found — He moved closer. Next week, we begin the actual work of healing old wounds that have been carried far longer than they should have been.
reflectionQuestions: What truth about being seen by God stayed with me this week?
Which broken place did I let God see this week, and how did it feel to be seen?
What do I want to carry into next week about God's nearness?

episodes.monthTheme: May, Healing: Restoring the Broken Places
episodes.weeklyIntroduction: Some wounds are decades old, carried quietly under a version of you that learned to function around the pain instead of through it. This week is about finally letting that healing begin.

days.scripture: "Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God." (Psalm 42:11, KJV)
days.truth: The psalmist talks to his own soul and tells it where to look. Healing reaches into the soul, not just the visible behavior.
days.affirmation: I am having my soul healed, not just my habits managed. God is working somewhere deeper than what other people can see.
days.sacredStep: Name one old wound today that you've only ever managed, never actually healed.

days.scripture: "And with his stripes we are healed." (Isaiah 53:5, KJV)
days.truth: Healing was already purchased at a cost I didn't have to pay myself.
days.affirmation: I am healed by what Christ already paid for. My old wound isn't waiting on me to earn its healing.
days.sacredStep: Speak this verse over your oldest wound today, by name if you can.

days.scripture: "For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them." (Isaiah 61:7, KJV)
days.truth: God doesn't only comfort what I feel. He promises to give back double for what shame took.
days.affirmation: I am believing God for more than relief. Where pain and shame took from me, He promises to return double.
days.sacredStep: Name one thing an old wound cost you, and ask God specifically to give it back.

days.scripture: "Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning." (Psalm 30:5, KJV)
days.truth: Grief has a season, but it isn't a permanent residence.
days.affirmation: I am allowed to weep for a night. Joy is still coming, even if this particular morning hasn't arrived yet.
days.sacredStep: Give yourself permission to grieve something today without rushing past it.

days.scripture: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest." (Matthew 11:28, KJV)
days.truth: Rest was offered directly to the exhausted, not to the already-healed.
days.affirmation: I am invited to bring my heavy load exactly as it is. I don't have to be lighter first to qualify for rest.
days.sacredStep: Bring one specific heavy thing to God in prayer today, using this exact invitation.

days.scripture: "The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped." (Psalm 28:7, KJV)
days.truth: Old wounds often taught me not to trust, but trust is still available and still worth practicing.
days.affirmation: I am helped when I trust, even wounds that once taught me otherwise are being slowly rewritten by that trust.
days.sacredStep: Practice trusting one person or God with something vulnerable today.

days.scripture: "For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the LORD." (Jeremiah 30:17, KJV)
days.truth: This promise is specific — health and wound-healing, named directly.
days.affirmation: I am being restored to health, and my wounds are being healed by the One who spoke this promise plainly.
